entries.behavior: Manage subscriptions exposes serialized import/export of modern reference container90 objects through the list owner, with an owned export child. Settings, complete query states, cached velocity/example-seed headers and both file/gallery histories survive JSON/PNG exchange, staged import and Apply/reopen. Casefold name collisions use (1) suffixes and every imported query gets a fresh history identity. JSON file export asks the original existing-path overwrite question; rejecting or closing the owner preserves the existing file. Format-specific JSON/PNG menu imports load one file at a time and retain accepted prefixes; cancellation leaves the saved store unchanged and stale callbacks cannot append or overwrite. Export reads current native queues plus draft reset/retry commands and preserves copied header metadata. Incomplete objects now ask the exact reference missing query log data title, message and import/back-out choices before they enter the draft; accepting persists empty logs and rejecting or cancelling continues remaining objects in list order. Apply is blocked while the question remains unanswered. Modern clipboard/JSON/PNG menu choices now dispatch their actual transport action. Legacy subscription type3 versions1–10 and legacy query1–3 import with full embedded histories, historical checker/limit defaults and fresh identity handling; obsolete gallery identifiers become the original paused unknown downloader. Actual Qt direct conversion and list exports constrain full upgraded payloads, apart from generated random identities. Fresh history names invalidate velocity/status according to SetQueryLogContainerName while retaining example/cached-count fields. Actual Reset/RetryFailed/RetryIgnored exports now refresh file-count/example caches without changing velocity or gallery examples. Retried files lose hashes exactly as SetStatus(UNKNOWN) does, in both detached exports and the real Apply transaction; reopening exports those persisted caches. Historical file seed-cache type8 versions1–7 now upgrade at the exchange boundary: versions1–4 retain only the first raw seed text, versions1–5 reset source timestamps, versions1–6 rewrite the old Tumblr spelling, and URL/path construction uses generic URL normalization. Primitive version1 note representations use Python spelling. Actual Qt payloads constrain ordered histories and derived count/example headers; modern containers embedding old caches also decode. Later duplicate identities that native queues cannot retain and complex/float Python note representations fail explicitly before staging rather than silently reduce history. Authored native count and persisted restore/reopen checks consume the recorded histories. Actual import menus now add permitted objects directly without an intermediate review child. Nested lists preserve object order; registered unrelated classes and primitives produce the original deduplicated type warning after valid objects stage. Per-file notices complete before the next file loads. Invalid or unreadable files retain their accepted prefix and stop the selected sequence; future-version errors warn once and continue later files. Missing-log rejection/dismissal continues the remaining objects, while the original information count includes permitted objects whose missing-log import was rejected. The last accepted subscription stays selected. Eleven actual Qt cases constrain notices, lists, selections and full exports; authored native replay reaches distinct persisted queue/history identities, exact ordered histories and reopening. Pickers execute outside the mutable owner borrow and recheck owner lifetime before staging returned paths.
